newsitem.title: INDIA: India's Bombay Customs to stay open on weekend.
newsitem.headline: India's Bombay Customs to stay open on weekend.

text.p: The Bombay Customs will stay open from April 12 to 14 to help clear export cargo which piled up following 10-day transport strike earlier this month, the president of Federation of Indian Export Organisations (FIEO) said on Saturday.
"The Bombay Customs last night notified exporters will be free to ship their consignments on these holidays," FIEO president Ramu Deora told Reuters.
The notification assured exporters their cargo will not be held up on account of any "discrepancies," he said.
The notification asks exporters to contact K.D Mankar, additonal commissioner of Bombay Customs, in case of any difficulty on 261 14 80 (office) or 412 34 92 (residence).
Deora, who is also president of All India Shippers' Council, said export cargo was clogging India's main ports.
India's monthly exports of about $3.0 billion was disrupted by the transport strike.
"I appeal to trade and industry to take advantage of the Customs' gesture and help regain the lost momentum in exports," Deora said.
